next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: District of Columbia Board of Elections — 2026 Elections

glance_notes.source_name: District of Columbia Board of Elections — Register to Vote
glance_notes.text: Same-Day Registration Available: District residents who miss the advance voter registration deadline may register and vote at any Vote Center during Early Voting or on Election Day. Same-day registrants must provide acceptable proof of District residency.

glance_notes.source_name: District of Columbia Board of Elections — 2026 General Election Calendar
glance_notes.text: Mail Ballots Sent Automatically: The District automatically mails a ballot to eligible registered voters for the General Election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the Board currently plans to begin mailing ballots on September 28.

glance_notes.source_name: District of Columbia Board of Elections — 2026 General Election Calendar
glance_notes.text: Early Voting October 26–November 1: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, Early Vote Centers are scheduled to operate every day from October 26 through November 1, from 8:30 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. Voters may use any Early Vote Center regardless of residential address.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible U.S. citizen residents of the District of Columbia may register online, by mail, email or fax, in person through the Board of Elections or another voter registration agency, or through same-day registration while voting. To qualify for federal and District-wide elections, a voter must be a U.S. citizen, reside in the District, not claim voting residence or the right to vote in another U.S. state or territory, and not have been found legally incompetent to vote by a court. District law permits preregistration beginning at age 16, although a person must satisfy the applicable age requirement before voting. The District also permits certain non-U.S.-citizen residents to register for eligible local elections, but noncitizens cannot vote for federal offices.
register.glance_value: Online, mail, email, fax, in person or same-day registration
register.source_name: District of Columbia Board of Elections — Register/Update Voter Registration
register.internal_note: DC is unusual because local law permits qualifying noncitizen District residents to participate in eligible local elections, while federal law prohibits noncitizens from voting for federal offices. Keep U.S.-citizen registration guidance distinct from the separate noncitizen local-election program. The Board's U.S.-citizen registration page states that a person may register beginning at age 16.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use the District of Columbia Board of Elections voter registration lookup to confirm registration status and voter information. Voters should check their residential and mailing information before ballots are mailed, particularly after moving. The Board's voter services also provide ballot tracking and Vote Center information during elections.
check_registration.glance_value: Check through the DC Board of Elections voter portal
check_registration.source_name: District of Columbia Board of Elections
check_registration.internal_note: Because DC automatically mails ballots to eligible registered voters, current registration and mailing information are particularly important. Same-day registration remains available if advance registration was not completed.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, voter registration applications and updates submitted online or by mail must be received by Tuesday, October 13. Applications submitted after the advance deadline are not processed for that election through the ordinary advance-registration process. Eligible District residents may still register and vote at an Early Vote Center from October 26 through November 1 or at any Election Day Vote Center on November 3 by providing acceptable proof of residence.
deadlines.glance_value: October 13 advance deadline; same-day registration remains available
deadlines.source_name: District of Columbia Board of Elections — 2026 General Election Calendar
deadlines.internal_note: The official 2026 General Election Calendar lists October 13 as the 21-day deadline for voter registration applications and updates other than certain in-person submissions. DCBOE independently confirms same-day registration during Early Voting and Election Day. Do not describe October 13 as an absolute final registration deadline.

polling_place.label: Find a Vote Center
polling_place.content: The District uses Vote Centers rather than requiring voters to use a single assigned Election Day polling place. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, a District voter may cast a ballot at any Election Day Vote Center regardless of residential address. Early voting likewise uses Early Vote Centers. Use the Board of Elections' official Vote Center information to find current locations.
polling_place.glance_value: Vote at any DC Vote Center
polling_place.source_name: District of Columbia Board of Elections — 2026 General Election Day Vote Centers
polling_place.internal_note: This is an important DC distinction. The official 2026 Election Day Vote Center page expressly states that voters may cast ballots at any Vote Center regardless of residential address. Do not tell DC voters they must report to an assigned precinct polling place.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: The District of Columbia General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Election Day Vote Centers are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. District voters may use any Election Day Vote Center regardless of residential address. Eligible residents may also complete same-day registration and cast a regular ballot after providing acceptable proof of residence. Voters who are in line at 8:00 p.m. are permitted to vote.
election_day.glance_value: 7:00 a.m. – 8:00 p.m.; use any Vote Center
election_day.source_name: District of Columbia Board of Elections — 2026 General Election Day Vote Centers
election_day.internal_note: The official 2026 General Election Calendar confirms that qualified electors may register and cast full ballots from 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. and that everyone in line at 8:00 p.m. may vote. Same-day registrants with proper proof of residence cast live regular ballots rather than automatically receiving provisional or special ballots.

polling_hours.label: Vote Center Hours
polling_hours.content: Election Day Vote Centers are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. on November 3, 2026. Voters who are in line when the Vote Centers close at 8:00 p.m. are permitted to cast a ballot.
polling_hours.internal_note: D.C. Official Code § 1-1001.10 establishes Election Day polling hours of 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. The Board's 2026 calendar independently confirms those hours.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, Early Vote Centers are scheduled to operate from Monday, October 26 through Sunday, November 1. They are open every day during that period from 8:30 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. Qualified voters may use any Early Vote Center regardless of residential address. Eligible residents who are not yet registered may also register and vote at an Early Vote Center by providing acceptable proof of District residence.
early_voting.source_name: District of Columbia Board of Elections — 2026 General Election Calendar
early_voting.internal_note: The Board's revised January 26, 2026 calendar explicitly gives October 26-November 1 and 8:30 a.m.-7:00 p.m. daily. Same-day registration is available at Early Vote Centers. Reverify locations close to the election because Vote Center lists can change.

absentee_mail.label: Mail-In & Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.content: The District automatically sends a mail-in ballot to eligible registered District voters, so voters normally do not need to request a ballot simply to vote by mail. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the Board currently plans to begin mailing ballots September 28. Voters who need a ballot sent somewhere other than their registered address may request an absentee ballot; the deadline for non-UOCAVA ballot requests is October 19. Official ballot drop boxes are available beginning October 9 at 11:00 a.m. and close at 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. Mailed ballots must be postmarked on or before November 3 and received by the Board by November 13 to be counted.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Ballots automatically mailed; Election Day postmark accepted through November 13
absentee_mail.source_name: District of Columbia Board of Elections — 2026 General Election Calendar
absentee_mail.flagged_reason: The September 28 ballot-mailing start is marked tentative in the official 2026 General Election Calendar. The statutory ballot-return deadlines are established, but the mailing-start date should be rechecked before publication.
absentee_mail.internal_note: DCBOE's accessibility guidance confirms that all eligible registered DC voters are sent a mail-in ballot. The 2026 calendar marks September 28 as the tentative beginning of ballot mailing, October 19 as the non-UOCAVA request deadline, October 9 at 11:00 a.m.-November 3 at 8:00 p.m. as the drop-box period, and November 13 as the receipt deadline for mailed ballots postmarked on or before Election Day. Drop-box ballots must be deposited by 8:00 p.m. Election Day.

voter_id.label: Voter ID & Proof of Residence
voter_id.content: Most already-registered District voters are not subject to a general photo-ID requirement simply to cast an in-person ballot. Identification or proof of residence is required in certain circumstances. A person completing same-day registration must provide acceptable proof showing the person's name and current District address. Acceptable documents include a current District DMV-issued identification, certain recent bank statements, utility bills, government checks or paychecks, a current lease, a homeless-shelter occupancy statement, a current District college tuition or housing statement, or another qualifying government document. Certain first-time voters who registered by mail or online may also be required to provide identification.
voter_id.glance_value: No general photo-ID rule; proof of residence required for same-day registration
voter_id.source_name: District of Columbia Board of Elections — Register/Update Voter Registration
voter_id.internal_note: Do not characterize DC as a photo-ID state. Same-day registration requires proof of residence, but qualifying documents include several non-photo records. Certain first-time voters whose identification information was not previously verified are subject to federal/HAVA identification requirements. A voter who fails an applicable ID requirement may have to use a Special Ballot.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: The District provides accessible voting options for voters with disabilities, senior voters and voters needing language assistance. Any voter may use any Vote Center during Early Voting or on Election Day, and accessible touchscreen voting equipment is available at Vote Centers. Voter Assistance Clerks are available to help. Curbside voting is available at Vote Centers for voters who cannot enter because of disability, seniority or illness. The District also provides an Accessible Remote Ballot Marking System that allows eligible voters with disabilities to mark a ballot privately and independently using compatible assistive technology.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible equipment, curbside voting and remote ballot marking
accessible_voting.source_name: District of Columbia Board of Elections — Accessible Voting and Language Access
accessible_voting.internal_note: Current DCBOE guidance expressly confirms accessible touchscreen equipment, Voter Assistance Clerks, curbside voting at all Vote Centers and the Accessible Remote Ballot Marking System. The ARB system supports major screen readers, tactile switches, closed captioning and audio-enabled systems.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: The District provides special absentee-voting procedures for eligible active-duty uniformed-service members, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living outside the United States under UOCAVA. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request an absentee ballot and may use the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot as a backup when eligible. Ballots may be delivered by mail, email or fax. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the Board must transmit timely requested UOCAVA ballots by September 18, and the deadline to request a UOCAVA ballot is October 31. Voted ballots returned electronically must be received by 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. Mailed UOCAVA ballots must be sent or postmarked by Election Day and received within the applicable post-election receipt period.
military_overseas.glance_value: UOCAVA ballots transmitted by September 18; request by October 31
military_overseas.source_name: District of Columbia Board of Elections — Military and Overseas Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: The official 2026 calendar sets September 18 as the 45-day UOCAVA transmission deadline and October 31 as the ballot-request deadline. DCBOE's current UOCAVA guidance says emailed or faxed voted ballots must arrive by 8:00 p.m. Election Day and mailed ballots must be sent on or before Election Day and received no later than the 10th day afterward. FPCA registration itself is subject to the 21-day registration deadline when used to register.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: A college student attending school in the District may register and vote in DC if the student meets the District's eligibility requirements and has resided in DC for at least 30 days before the election. A District college or university housing statement or tuition bill for the current term may serve as proof of residence for registration. Students using a campus address should include their residence hall on the registration application. A DC resident attending college elsewhere may remain registered in DC and vote using the District's mail or absentee procedures when eligible.
student_voting.glance_value: DC college residence may qualify after 30 days
student_voting.source_name: District of Columbia Board of Elections — College & High School Students FAQ
student_voting.internal_note: DCBOE specifically states that a college student attending school in DC may register if the student has resided in the District for 30 days before the election. A college/university housing statement can establish the DC address. Do not imply that merely attending a DC college automatically establishes voting residency.

sample_ballot.label: Official Ballot Information
sample_ballot.content: The District of Columbia Board of Elections publishes official General Election candidate information and sample ballot materials. Ballot contents vary according to ward, Advisory Neighborhood Commission single-member district and voter eligibility. Voters should use the Board's official 2026 General Election resources to review the ballot that applies to them once final sample ballots are published.
sample_ballot.source_name: District of Columbia Board of Elections — 2026 Elections
sample_ballot.internal_note: The official General Election calendar permits publication of a sample copy of the official ballot beginning October 13. The 2026 Elections page already provides General Election candidate and ANC candidate information. Reverify final sample ballots after publication because ward and ANC contests differ by address.

contact.label: Contact the Election Authority
contact.content: District of Columbia Board of Elections, 1015 Half Street SE, Suite 750, Washington, DC 20003. Phone: 202-727-2525. Toll-free voter information line: 866-328-6837. Fax: 202-347-2648. For voter registration, ballot, Vote Center, accessibility or other election questions, contact the District of Columbia Board of Elections.
contact.source_name: District of Columbia Board of Elections
contact.internal_note: Current DCBOE materials verify 1015 Half Street SE, Suite 750, Washington, DC 20003; 202-727-2525; fax 202-347-2648; and the toll-free voter service 1-866-DCVOTES / 866-328-6837. No uncertain general email address was inserted into reader-facing content.

official_resources.label: Official District Resources
official_resources.content: Use the District of Columbia Board of Elections for official election information. DCBOE provides voter registration, registration lookup, Vote Center and ballot drop-box locations, mail-ballot information, ballot tracking, accessible voting services, military and overseas voting guidance, candidate information, sample ballots, election calendars and results. Unlike states where election administration is divided among counties, the District's elections are administered centrally by the DC Board of Elections.
